subject.title: Feature: Allow cron heartbeat interval to vary based on state conditions (deadline-aware scheduling)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class conditional cadence contract beyond merged cron event triggers, and should that contract include heartbeat scheduling?
rationale: The source gap is narrow enough to identify, but choosing condition language, state sources, trigger-vs-schedule semantics, and heartbeat scope is product/API direction rather than a safe autonomous fix.

options.title: Scope a narrow conditional cadence contract
options.body: Keep the issue open and define cron-only or cron-plus-heartbeat acceptance criteria before any implementation touches protocol, config, persistence, docs, and tests.

options.title: Treat event triggers as sufficient
options.body: Document a deadline-aware trigger recipe and close this after maintainers confirm polling overhead and static heartbeat cadence are acceptable.

options.title: Defer first-class cadence
options.body: Leave the feature unscheduled until stronger user evidence justifies expanding the scheduler surface beyond the existing trigger mechanism.

recommendation.title: Scope a narrow conditional cadence contract
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and define cron-only or cron-plus-heartbeat acceptance criteria before any implementation touches protocol, config, persistence, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the current trigger-script design and has the strongest recent history across cron and heartbeat scheduling surfaces.
